english: Let $D_1$ be the set of all real numbers $x$ for which $\log_e\left(\dfrac{2x^{2}-5x-7}{x^{2}-2x-8}\right)$ is defined, and let $D_2$ be the set of all real numbers $x$ for which $\log_e\left(2x^{2}-5x-7\right)-\log_e\left(x^{2}-2x-8\right)$ is defined. Let $f:D_1\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:D_2\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\log_e\left(\dfrac{2x^{2}-5x-7}{x^{2}-2x-8}\right)$ and $g(x)=\log_e\left(2x^{2}-5x-7\right)-\log_e\left(x^{2}-2x-8\right)$. Let $S$ be the set of all $x\in D_1$ such that either $x\notin D_2$ or $f(x)\ne g(x)$. Then the sum of the lengths of the intervals that make up $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $D_1$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $\log_e\left(\dfrac{2x^{2}-5x-7}{x^{2}-2x-8}\right)$ परिभाषित है, तथा $D_2$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $\log_e\left(2x^{2}-5x-7\right)-\log_e\left(x^{2}-2x-8\right)$ परिभाषित है। माना कि $f:D_1\to\mathbb{R}$ तथा $g:D_2\to\mathbb{R}$ क्रमशः $f(x)=\log_e\left(\dfrac{2x^{2}-5x-7}{x^{2}-2x-8}\right)$ तथा $g(x)=\log_e\left(2x^{2}-5x-7\right)-\log_e\left(x^{2}-2x-8\right)$ द्वारा परिभाषित हैं। माना कि $S$ उन सभी $x\in D_1$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए या तो $x\notin D_2$ है या $f(x)\ne g(x)$ है। तब $S$ को बनाने वाले अन्तरालों की लम्बाइयों का योग ______ है।
solution: $D_2$: both factors positive: $\left(x<-1\text{ or }x>\dfrac72\right)$ and $(x<-2\text{ or }x>4)\Rightarrow(-\infty,-2)\cup(4,\infty)$
On $D_2$ both arguments are positive, so $\log_e\dfrac AB=\log_e A-\log_e B$: $f=g$ there
$S=D_1\setminus D_2=\left(-1,\dfrac72\right)$ (both numerator and denominator negative), length $\dfrac92=4.5$
solution_full: Factorise: $2x^{2}-5x-7=(2x-7)(x+1)$ and $x^{2}-2x-8=(x-4)(x+2)$. The critical points in increasing order are $-2,\,-1,\,\dfrac72,\,4$.

$D_1$ needs $\dfrac{(2x-7)(x+1)}{(x-4)(x+2)}>0$. By the sign scheme the expression is positive on $(-\infty,-2)$, negative on $(-2,-1)$, positive on $\left(-1,\dfrac72\right)$, negative on $\left(\dfrac72,4\right)$ and positive on $(4,\infty)$. So $D_1=(-\infty,-2)\cup\left(-1,\dfrac72\right)\cup(4,\infty)$.
$D_2$ needs both $(2x-7)(x+1)>0$, i.e. $x<-1$ or $x>\dfrac72$, and $(x-4)(x+2)>0$, i.e. $x<-2$ or $x>4$. Together: $D_2=(-\infty,-2)\cup(4,\infty)$, a subset of $D_1$.

For $x\in D_2$, $A=2x^{2}-5x-7>0$ and $B=x^{2}-2x-8>0$, so $\log_e\dfrac AB=\log_e A-\log_e B$ and $f(x)=g(x)$. Hence the condition $f(x)\ne g(x)$ never holds on $D_2$, and $f$ and $g$ are identical as functions only when both are restricted to $D_2$.
Therefore $S=D_1\setminus D_2=\left(-1,\dfrac72\right)$: there both $A$ and $B$ are negative, so the quotient is positive but the separate logarithms are undefined.
$S$ is a single interval of length $\dfrac72-(-1)=\dfrac92=4.5$ (a Monte Carlo estimate on $[-10,10]$ gives about $4.46$).
originality_note: New: the gap between the domains of log(A/B) and log A - log B, measured as a length, with factors chosen so that the gap is an interior interval where both factors are negative (way 5). Closest known: 'are log(x^2) and 2 log x identical' type questions. Different because: the student must run a four-point sign scheme for D1 and an intersection of two conditions for D2, and justify that the functions agree on D2.

concept_use.Miscellaneous concepts of Functions: Sign scheme (wavy-curve method) of a rational expression with four critical points gives D1, and the two separate conditions give D2.
concept_use.Definition of a function; vertical line: f and g are compared as functions: they agree wherever both are defined, so they fail to be identical exactly on D1 \ D2, whose length is the answer.

stem_review: Read as a student: both domains defined explicitly as sets of real x where the expressions make sense; S defined without hinting that f=g on D2; 'sum of the lengths of the intervals' is robust even though S is one interval. Answer 4.5 checked with sympy set algebra and Monte Carlo. Positive decimal as planned. Changed: replaced 'the length of the interval S' by 'the sum of the lengths of the intervals that make up S' so the stem does not reveal that S is one interval.
key_step: Separating where the quotient is positive (four-point sign scheme) from where both factors are positive, and seeing that the difference is the interval where both are negative.
justification: A routine sign-scheme chain plus the identical-functions comparison; the trap (both factors negative) is common, but the numerical format with two domains and a set definition adds checking. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q8 (L2) for domain-type counting, nudged up by format; near 2025-P2-Q3 (L3).
blueprint_concepts: Definition of a function; vertical line test; identical functions
